005package org.wpilib.util.option;
006
007import static org.wpilib.util.ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam;
008
009import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
010import java.util.Optional;
011import java.util.function.Function;
012import java.util.function.Predicate;
013import java.util.function.Supplier;
014import java.util.stream.Stream;
015
016/**
017 * Represents a value that may or may not be present. Options are useful for handling data that may
018 * or may not be present without risking potential NullPointerExceptions or NoSuchElementExceptions.
019 *
020 * <p>This interface is intended to be used with pattern-matching {@code if} and {@code switch}
021 * statements, a Java language feature introduced in Java 21. See the <a
022 * href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/language/record-patterns.html">official Java
023 * documentation</a> for more information on this language feature.
024 *
025 * <pre>{@code
026 * // Usage in if statements:
027 * Option<String> potentialText = fetchData(); // Pretend this function exists for sake of example
028 * if (potentialText instanceof Some(String text)) {
029 *   System.out.println("Got text: " + text);
030 * } else {
031 *   System.err.println("Didn't get any text");
032 * }
033 *
034 * // Usage in switch statements:
035 * switch (potentialText) {
036 *   case Some(String text) -> System.out.println("Got text: " + text);
037 *   case None() -> System.err.println("Didn't get any text");
038 * }
039 * }</pre>
040 *
041 * @param <T> The type of the values that can potentially be stored in the option
042 * @see <a
043 *     href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/language/record-patterns.html">https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/language/record-patterns.html</a>
044 */
045public sealed interface Option<T> permits Some, None {
046  /**
047   * Creates a new option wrapping a value. An exception is thrown if the value is null. If you want
048   * to safely handle values that are possibly null, use {@link Option#ofNullable(Object)} instead.
049   *
050   * @param value The value to wrap. Cannot be null.
051   * @param <T> The type of the values that can potentially be stored in the option
052   * @return An option for the value.
053   * @throws NullPointerException if {@code value} is {@code null}
054   */
055  static <T> Option<T> some(T value) {
056    return Some.of(value);
057  }
058
059  /**
060   * Creates an empty option containing no data.
061   *
062   * @param <T> The type of values that could have potentially been stored in the option
063   * @return A no-value option
064   */
065  static <T> None<T> none() {
066    return None.none();
067  }
068
069  /**
070   * Creates an option wrapping a potentially null value. If the value is null, an empty {@link
071   * None} value is returned, otherwise a {@link Some} wrapping the non-null value is returned.
072   *
073   * @param value The value to wrap. May be null.
074   * @param <T> The type of values that can be stored in the option
075   * @return An option corresponding to the given nullable value
076   */
077  static <T> Option<T> ofNullable(T value) {
078    if (value != null) {
079      return new Some<>(value);
080    } else {
081      return none();
082    }
083  }
084
085  /**
086   * Creates a new option corresponding to a {@code java.util.Optional} object. If the optional is
087   * {@link Optional#isPresent() present}, a {@link Some} is option is returned; otherwise, a {@link
088   * None} option is returned.
089   *
090   * @param javaOptional The Java {@code Optional} object to wrap. Cannot be null.
091   * @param <T> The type of the values that can potentially be stored in the option.
092   * @return An option for the optional value.
093   */
094  static <T> Option<T> ofOptional(Optional<? extends T> javaOptional) {
095    requireNonNullParam(javaOptional, "javaOptional", "Option.ofOptional");
096
097    if (javaOptional.isPresent()) {
098      return new Some<>(javaOptional.get());
099    } else {
100      return none();
101    }
102  }
103
104  /**
105   * Gets the value of this option, falling back to {@code fallbackValue} if the option is empty.
106   *
107   * @param fallbackValue The default fallback value. Cannot be null.
108   * @return The value of this option, if present, or the fallback value.
109   * @throws NullPointerException if {@code fallbackValue} is {@code null}
110   */
111  T orElse(T fallbackValue);
112
113  /**
114   * Gets the value of this option, falling back to a value provided by {@code supplier} if the
115   * option is empty.
116   *
117   * @param fallbackSupplier A supplier for fallback values. Cannot be null, and cannot return
118   *     nulls.
119   * @return The value of this option, if present, or a fallback value provided by {@code
120   *     fallbackSupplier}.
121   * @throws NullPointerException if {@code supplier} is {@code null}
122   * @throws NullPointerException if {@code supplier} returns {@code null}
123   */
124  T orElseGet(Supplier<? extends T> fallbackSupplier);
125
126  /**
127   * Gets the value of this option, throwing an exception if the option is empty.
128   *
129   * @return The value of this option, if present
130   * @throws NoSuchElementException if the option is empty
131   */
132  T orElseThrow();
133
134  /**
135   * Gets the value of this option, throwing an exception if the option is empty.
136   *
137   * @param exceptionSupplier A provider for an exception to throw if the option is empty. Cannot be
138   *     {@code null} and cannot return a {@code null} exception.
139   * @param <X> The type of the exception to throw if the option is empty.
140   * @return The value of this option, if present.
141   * @throws X if the option is empty
142   */
143  <X extends Throwable> T orElseThrow(Supplier<? extends X> exceptionSupplier) throws X;
144
145  /**
146   * If a value is present, returns an option holding the value, otherwise returns an option
147   * provided by the supplying function.
148   *
149   * @param supplier the supplying function that produces an option to return if this option is
150   *     empty.
151   * @return this option, if a value is present, or an option provided by the supplying function if
152   *     no value is present
153   * @throws NullPointerException if {@code supplier} is {@code null} or it returns a {@code null}
154   *     value
155   */
156  Option<T> or(Supplier<? extends Option<? extends T>> supplier);
157
158  /**
159   * Returns an option describing the value of this option if it matches the given predicate.
160   * Otherwise, returns an empty option.
161   *
162   * @param predicate The predicate to test the value against. Must not be null.
163   * @return An option containing the original value if the predicate is satisfied, or an empty
164   *     option if the predicate is not satisfied or if this option is empty.
165   * @throws NullPointerException if {@code predicate} is {@code null}
166   */
167  Option<T> filter(Predicate<? super T> predicate);
168
169  /**
170   * Applies a mapping function to the value in this option, returning a new option containing the
171   * result of the mapping function. The function may return {@code null}; if so, an empty option is
172   * returned. Applying a mapping function to an empty option always returns another empty option.
173   * This function is equivalent to the following switch statement:
174   *
175   * <pre>{@code
176   * Option<?> option = ...;
177   * Option<?> mapped = switch (option) {
178   *   case Some(var value) -> Option.of(mappingFunction.apply(value));
179   *   case None() -> Option.none();
180   * };
181   * }</pre>
182   *
183   * @param mapper The mapping function to apply.
184   * @param <R> The result type of the mapping function
185   * @return An option containing the result of the mapping operation, or an empty option if the
186   *     mapping function returned null
187   * @throws NullPointerException if {@code mapper} is {@code null}
188   */
189  <R> Option<R> map(Function<? super T, ? extends R> mapper);
190
191  /**
192   * Like {@link #map(Function)}, but where the function may return another {@code Option} object
193   * instead of a raw value. Useful to avoid stackups of nested {@code Option<Option<Option<...>>>}
194   * types.
195   *
196   * @param mapper The mapping function to apply
197   * @param <R> The result type of the mapping function
198   * @return An option containing the result of the mapping operation
199   */
200  <R> Option<R> flatMap(Function<? super T, ? extends Option<? extends R>> mapper);
201
202  /**
203   * If a value is present, returns a sequential {@link Stream} containing only that value,
204   * otherwise returns an empty {@code Stream}.
205   *
206   * <p>This method can be used to transform a {@code Stream} of option elements to a {@code Stream}
207   * of present value elements:
208   *
209   * <pre>{@code
210   * Stream<Option<T>> os = ..
211   * Stream<T> s = os.flatMap(Option::stream)
212   * }</pre>
213   *
214   * @return the optional value as a {@code Stream}
215   */
216  Stream<T> stream();
217}
